text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike on /v1/generate (us-west-2) — SLO burn 14% over 5m. Paging @eng-oncall :rotating_light:
anna-oncall: acked. looking now, grabbing dashboards and traces.
marc: seeing a tail spike on the inference pool (dedicated-gpu-03). p99 up to 2.6s, p95 at ~800ms.
priya: any recent deploys?
josh: no deploys in the last 30m. autoscaler shows no additional pods added — curls to the /metrics endpoint show high queue depth.
ops-bot: autoscale:policy=no_action reason="scale inhibited by cooldown" current_replicas=6 target_replicas=10
anna-oncall: ok. quick mitigation idea: route low-priority traffic to cheaper model variant and warm a new dedicated node pool. can someone flip routing policy?
marc: I can flip route. runbook snippet: 
```
# temp route to fallback-model-v2
POST /routing/reconfigure
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "priority": "low -> fallback-model-v2"
}
```
priya: +1 to routing, but customer-impact first — which customers hit p99?
sarah-cs: we have a spike in support tickets for two enterprise customers (acme-corp, betta-ai). both report slower response times in-app. I'll start a customer DM and flag for status page.
josh: executing route change now. will post output.
ops-bot: routing: change requested by josh status=ok details="route updated, 22% of traffic remapped to fallback-model-v2"
marc: initiating warmup of an extra dedicated node pool (region us-west-2). running: gcloud/scale up --pool dedicated-gpu-ww-2 --count 4
anna-oncall: good. while that comes up, can we reduce batch size on tail-heavy requests? that should lower tail latency for interactive flows.
josh: lowered max_batch_tokens from 2048 -> 512 on gateway config. config reload succeeded.
incident-bot: NOTE: p99 decreased from 2.6s -> 1.4s in 90s after config changes. SLO burn now 6% over 5m.
priya: traces show a few hotkeys — redis KV evictions. marc, can you check k-v cache evict metrics?
marc: kvcache:evict-rate spiked 5x, memory pressure on sidecar. evict target increased. working on prefix pinning for top keys.
sarah-cs: told customers we're investigating and applied mitigations; ETA for full fix 15-25m. they want an incident summary when resolved.
anna-oncall: filing short incident note in the tracker: "latency spike caused by combined autoscaler cooldown + KV eviction hotkeys — mitigated via routing fallback, batch size reduction, and scale-up."
ops-bot: compute:pool dedicated-gpu-ww-2 status=provisioning ETA=4m
josh: verifying telemetry — p95 stable ~420ms, p99 trending down to ~900ms.
incident-bot: REMINDER: PagerDuty escalation suppressed (manual ack).
priya: once pool is ready, we'll drain the warmup traffic into it and revert routing change. plan: (1) finish warmup, (2) migrate heavy customers back with canary, (3) monitor SLO for 10m.
marc: pool ready. running canary migration for acme-corp traffic shard.
ops-bot: canary:acme status=ok migrated=5% -> 25%
anna-oncall: observing metrics for the canary — no regression so far. increasing to 60%.
josh: rolling back batch size to original for tenants unaffected by hotkeys to regain throughput.
incident-bot: UPDATE: p99 stabilized at ~420-700ms across shards; SLO burn down to 1.2% over 5m.
sarah-cs: customers acknowledged the update, acme asked for postmortem.
anna-oncall: marking thread as incident-in-progress -> mitigation-complete. will create postmortem template and assign to marc/priya.
priya: noted. I'll own root cause analysis on KV eviction tuning and propose a soft-limit on autoscaler cooldown triggers.
marc: I'll follow up with telemetry for hotkey detection and prefix pinning rollout.
incident-bot: RESOLVED: p99 latency normalized; no active paging. incident duration ~28m.
anna-oncall: thanks everyone. quick follow-ups: 1) update runbook with autoscale cooldown caveat, 2) add hotkey alerts for kvcache, 3) customer-facing summary draft.
sarah-cs: drafting customer summary now and will post to status.redwood.ai when ready. :white_check_mark:
anna-oncall: closing thread once postmortem is created. good job team. :clap:
